section: 3.7 Testing Stage 5: Bijective Normalizing Flows Downstream of OLEE (Flow-SiMR-V)
text:
3.7 Testing Stage 5: Bijective Normalizing Flows Downstream of OLEE (Flow-SiMR-V)
Stage 5 of our deductive progression pairs the OLEE bottleneck \(\mathbf{V}_m\) with volume-preserving RealNVP normalizing flows \(f_{\text{flow},m}: \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k\).

3.7.1 Empirical Verification of Detached-Prior Subspace Decoupling
As proved in Chapter 2 (Stage 5) and Appendix C, backpropagating Gaussian prior log-likelihood gradients (\(\nabla_{\mathbf{V}_m} \mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\)) through a rectangular Stiefel projection (\(k \ll p_m\)) lacks a subspace log-determinant term and drives \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto the trailing (smallest-eigenvalue) noise eigenvectors of \(\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m\). Enforcing detached-prior subspace decoupling (\(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})\) at the prior boundary, coupled with iteration-0 linear Stiefel warm start and zero-initialized identity coupling layers):

Raises Flow-SiMR-V out-of-sample CogPC1 R^2 on ADNI-MCI (Protocol B) from \(0.0369\) (collapsed trailing-eigenvector subspace) to \(0.2341\) at \(k=3\) (\(0.2966\) at \(k=6\), a \(+704\%\) improvement).
Propels Flow-SiMR-V to #3 overall Friedman rank across all 12 benchmark datasets (Consensus Rank \(4.17\), OLEE Basis Rank \(4.12\), #1 real-cohort consensus mean \(0.627\)), achieving the #1 consensus accuracy on mfeat (\(81.9\%\)), #1 on TCGA-KIRC (\(69.7\%\)), and #1 on Polynomial (\(R^2 = 0.925\)).



3.7.2 Delayed MAI Gating Stability under Rogue Noise Views
We further evaluate Flow-SiMR-V with Delayed MAI Gating Warmup under two rogue-noise stress tests: a 4-view mixed non-linear sinusoidal benchmark containing a pure Gaussian noise view (Table 3.7) and the 4-view TCGA-BRCA clinical multi-omics cohort with an injected Gaussian noise view (\(N = 1,010\), Table 3.8).

title: 4  Discussion
text:
4.1 Deductive Synthesis Across the Five Methodological Stages
Integrating heterogeneous, high-dimensional observations remains a fundamental task in computational anatomy, neurodegenerative disease modeling, and translational molecular oncology (Stone et al. 2020; Avants et al. 2021). As diagnostic and clinical trial cohorts incorporate multi-sequence structural and diffusion MRI, molecular positron emission tomography, biofluid assays, and high-throughput transcriptomics (Weiner et al. 2017; Jack et al. 2008; Marek et al. 2011), representation learning methods must balance the capacity to model non-linear manifold geometry against the legal, ethical, and scientific necessity for verifiable physical biomarker attribution (Holmberg et al. 2022). In neurotrauma, blast-induced shockwaves produce diffuse microstructural shearing across white matter tracts that demands sparse, signed decomposition without cancellation artifacts (Stone et al. 2024). In cancer genomics, resolving functional oncogenic pathways across somatic copy-number alterations, mRNA expression, and targeted protein arrays in breast carcinoma (BRCA) (The Cancer Genome Atlas Network 2012; Cancer Discovery 2016) and clear cell renal cell carcinoma (KIRC) (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network 2013) requires multi-modal alignment that preserves exact gene-level attribution.
In this work, we formulated multi-view representation learning deductively across five methodological stages governed by the Only Linear Encoder Entrypoint (OLEE) contract (Chapter 2) and evaluated every stage empirically across 12 multi-modal data regimes (6 real clinical/genomic/imaging cohorts and 6 synthetic manifolds across 3 random seeds, totaling 324 model evaluations), alongside a 1,214-combination hyperparameter sweep and a 10-seed mediation study in Alzheimer’s disease (\(N=1,084\)).
Our theoretical and empirical results demonstrate how each of the five methodological stages resolves a distinct failure mode in multi-view representation learning:

title: 4  Discussion
text:
Stage 1 — The Input Boundary (OLEE & NSA-Flow Manifold Geometry): Restricting the entrypoint of each modality \(m\) to the compact Stiefel manifold (\(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m, \mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{I}_k\)) guarantees globally constant attribution derivatives (\(\nabla_{\mathbf{X}_m} \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{V}_m\)) and closed-form counterfactual recourse (\(\delta \mathbf{x}_m^* = \Delta \mathbf{z}_m^* \mathbf{V}_m^\top\)) (Pearl 2009; Wachter et al. 2017). Coupling the Stiefel constraint with the Non-negative Stiefel Approximating Flow (nsa_flow) enforces zero signed lobe crosstalk (\(\|\mathbf{V}_m^+ \odot \mathbf{V}_m^-\|_1 = 0\)) and recovers localized sparse feature supports (SiMLR-LBFGSB \(F_1 = 0.991\), SiMLR-LBFGS \(0.966\), LEND \(0.899\), Flow-SiMR-V \(0.826\)) where rotationally invariant PCA fails (\(F_1 = 0.333\)).
Stage 2 — Cross-View Consensus, Bipartite Topologies & Spectral Triage (MAI): Cross-view alignment isolates shared biological variance when single-matrix concatenation is overwhelmed by view-private noise (Shared+Private: LEND \(R^2 = 0.949, CMC = 0.896\) and Flow-SiMR-V \(R^2 = 0.845, CMC = 0.880\) vs. PCA \(R^2 = 0.639, CMC = 0.636\)). Crucially, when predictor views are aligned against a training-only clinical target view via a bipartite graph (Protocol B on ADNI-MCI, {0:[3], 1:[3], 2:[3], 3:[0,1,2]}), the predictor bases \(\mathbf{V}_m\) are steered directly toward the disease axis without requiring clinical labels at test time (CogPC1 R^2 \(= 0.224\text{–}0.241\) vs. \(0.152\) for PCA).
Stage 3 — Linear Multi-View Manifold Solvers & Iteration-0 Warm Start (SiMLR, SiMLR-LBFGS, SiMLR-LBFGSB): Bound-constrained quasi-Newton optimization (SiMLR-LBFGSB) and Riemannian L-BFGS (SiMLR-LBFGS) achieve the #1 and #2 global Friedman ranks on the strictly linear OLEE basis probe across all 12 datasets (\(3.17\) and \(4.00\); #1 and #2 on the 6 real-world cohorts with mean ranks \(2.50\) and \(3.33\)), while providing the fast iteration-0 linear warm start for all deep and flow architectures.
Stage 4 — Non-Linear Decoding Downstream of OLEE (LEND vs. NED / NEDPP): Keeping the encoder strictly linear (\(\mathbf{Z}_m = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m\)) while placing non-linear MLP capacity exclusively in the decoder (LEND) achieves the #1 global Friedman rank on consensus prediction (\(3.58\), mean \(0.760 \pm 0.249\)) and the highest latent coordinate recovery (\(CMC = 0.907\)). Conversely, inserting MLP layers inside the encoder (NED rank \(7.29\), NEDPP rank \(8.04\)) causes severe overfitting in sample-limited cohorts (\(p_{\text{Holm}} \le 7.5 \times 10^{-4}\)).
Stage 5 — Bijective Normalizing Flows & Detached-Prior Subspace Decoupling (Flow-SiMR-V): We proved that backpropagating standard Gaussian prior log-likelihood gradients (\(\nabla_{\mathbf{V}_m} \mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\)) through a rectangular Stiefel projection (\(k \ll p_m\)) lacks a subspace log-determinant term and drives \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto the trailing (smallest-eigenvalue) noise eigenvectors of \(\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m\). Detaching the prior gradient at the OLEE boundary (\(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})\)) resolves this collapse, boosting Flow-SiMR-V CogPC1 R^2 on ADNI-MCI by \(+704\%\) (from \(0.0369\) to \(0.2966\) at \(k=6\), \(0.2341\) at \(k=3\)) and elevating Flow-SiMR-V to #3 overall rank across all 12 benchmark datasets while preserving exact analytical invertibility, conditional cross-view imputation, and geodesic trajectory mapping.

title: 4  Discussion
section: 4.3 Why Cognitive Mediation and Bipartite Alignment Multiply ADNI-MCI Prediction
text:
4.3 Why Cognitive Mediation and Bipartite Alignment Multiply ADNI-MCI Prediction
Our investigation of \(N = 1,084\) patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) from the ADNI cohort (Weiner et al. 2017; Jack et al. 2008) highlights two general methodological principles for clinical neuroimaging:

Bipartite Target Alignment (Protocol B) vs. Unsupervised Anatomical Alignment (Protocol A): When the three structural MRI views (\(382\) features) are aligned only with each other (Protocol A), their top shared components reflect global brain size and healthy aging rather than cognitive decline (PCA CogPC1 R^2 \(= 0.1522\)). Aligning each MRI view directly against the 11 \(>98\%\)-complete cognitive measures during training via a bipartite graph ({0:[3], 1:[3], 2:[3], 3:[0,1,2]})—while withholding View 4 at test time—steers the MRI projections \(\mathbf{V}_0, \mathbf{V}_1, \mathbf{V}_2\) onto the cortical atrophy signature of cognitive impairment, raising MRI-only test CogPC1 R^2 to \(0.2237\) (SiMLR-LBFGSB, 3-seed mean) and \(0.2407\) (SiMLR-Lookahead in the 1,214-combination sweep).
Over 6-Fold Gain on Functional Dementia Severity (CDR-SB) via Cognitive Mediation: Trying to predict daily functional disability (CDR-SB) directly from the 382 brain MRI features explains only 4.1% of test variance (\(R^2 = 0.0411 \pm 0.0248\)). Biologically, hippocampal and cortical tissue loss first erodes mental abilities (memory recall, executive attention), and that loss of mental ability impairs daily functioning (\(84.5\%\text{–}86.4\%\) indirect effect, Sobel \(p < 10^{-15}\)). Modeling this two-step pathway (\(\text{Brain MRI} \to \text{Cognition} \to \text{CDR-SB}\)) increases out-of-sample CDR-SB accuracy over six-fold (LEND-SiMR + MAI: \(R^2 = 0.2648 \pm 0.0332\); SiMLR: \(R^2 = 0.2443 \pm 0.0534\) in \(0.86\text{s}\)), whereas unconstrained deep encoders (NED-SiMR + MAI: \(R^2 = 0.1127\)) overfit the 382 anatomical features.

title: 4  Discussion
section: 4.4 Clinical Translation Across Cohorts and Translational Pathology
text:
4.4 Clinical Translation Across Cohorts and Translational Pathology
The modular Deep SiMLR framework addresses distinct clinical and biological challenges across the six real-world cohorts:

Cleveland Heart Disease (Heart, \(N=297\)): Integrating resting vitals (\(p_1 = 7\)) and stress electrocardiography (\(p_2 = 6\)) achieves \(84.8\%\) strictly linear probe accuracy (NSAFlow-PCA) and \(83.7\%\) consensus accuracy (NSAFlow-PCA, PCA, SiMLR-LBFGSB), directly attributing risk to exercise-induced ST depression (oldpeak), maximum heart rate (thalach), and chest pain type (cp).
Diabetes Progression (Diabetes, \(N=442\)): Integrating anthropometric/hemodynamic baselines (\(p_1 = 5\)) and serum lipid chemistries (\(p_2 = 5\)), NSAFlow-PCA (\(R^2 = 0.382\)) and SiMLR-LBFGSB / SiMLR-LBFGS (linear probe \(R^2 = 0.396\)) outperform dense PCA (\(0.350\)) while isolating body mass index (bmi) and serum triglycerides (s5).
Breast and Renal Translational Oncology (TCGA-BRCA \(N=822\), TCGA-KIRC \(N=467\)): Enforcing \(\ge 98\%\) completeness across mRNA (\(p_1=200\)), CNV (\(p_2=150\)), and RPPA proteomics (\(p_3=150\)), NSAFlow-PCA (\(92.7\%\)), SiMLR-LBFGSB (\(92.6\%\) linear probe), and LEND (\(92.6\%\) linear probe, \(92.2\%\) consensus) accurately stratify Estrogen Receptor status in BRCA, while Flow-SiMR-V and LEND lead pathologic stage classification in KIRC (\(69.7\%\)).
High-Cardinality Multi-View Pattern Recognition (mfeat, \(N=2,000\)): Across 4 heterogeneous descriptor views, Flow-SiMR-V (\(81.9\%\)) and LEND (\(78.9\%\)) lead 3D consensus classification, while SiMLR-LBFGSB (\(94.8\%\)) and NEDPP (\(96.2\%\)) outperform concatenated PCA (\(72.7\%\)) by over \(+22\) percentage points on the OLEE basis probe.
Neurotrauma and Longitudinal Parkinson’s Cohorts (TBI & PPMI): In blast-induced diffuse axonal injury (Stone et al. 2024) and longitudinal dopaminergic imaging (Marek et al. 2011), NSAFlow-PCA and SiMLR-LBFGSB enforce disjoint non-negative support (\(\mathbf{V}^+ \odot \mathbf{V}^- = \mathbf{0}\)), isolating tract-specific white matter shearing and striatal binding changes without destructive sign cancellation.

title: 4  Discussion
section: 4.5 Methodological Principles for Multi-Modal Biomedical Studies
text:
4.5 Methodological Principles for Multi-Modal Biomedical Studies
Our experiments establish four general methodological rules for multi-modal biomedical benchmarks:

In-Fold Preprocessing & Covariate Residualization: Scaling, feature selection, and Frisch–Waugh–Lovell covariate residualization must be fitted strictly on the training fold and projected onto the test fold.
Completeness Hygiene (\(\ge 98\%\)) Before Multi-View Alignment: Sparse clinical or genomic variables with high missingness must be filtered before median imputation so constant-imputed columns cannot corrupt cross-view covariance matrices.
Bipartite Target Topologies for Partial-View Clinical Deployment: When a target view is present during training but absent at deployment, aligning predictor views exclusively to the target view via a bipartite graph topology prevents background inter-predictor covariance from dominating the learned basis.
Detached-Prior Subspace Decoupling for Bottlenecked Normalizing Flows: Whenever a normalizing flow operates downstream of a rectangular Stiefel projection (\(k \ll p_m\)), the Gaussian prior log-likelihood must be detached at the linear boundary (\(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})\)) so prior gradients cannot drive \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto trailing noise eigenvectors.

title: 4  Discussion
section: 4.6 Limitations
text:
4.6 Limitations

First-Layer Linear Constraint: Restricting the input layer to an orthogonal Stiefel projection limits the model’s ability to capture high-order intra-modality non-linear feature interactions directly at the raw pixel or token level.
Latent Dimension Scaling: Exact Stiefel retractions and polar factorizations scale cubically with latent rank (\(\mathcal{O}(k^3)\)). While fast for typical biomedical latent ranks (\(k \le 64\)), scaling to \(k > 500\) requires block-Stiefel approximations.
Sample Size in Clinical Sub-Cohorts: While \(B = 12\) dataset blocks (\(324\) evaluations) provide strong non-parametric power (\(\chi_F^2 = 30.77\text{–}32.06, p \le 1.54 \times 10^{-4}\)), fine-grained differences among top OLEE variants on small single-center cohorts benefit from paired permutation and multi-seed cross-validation.

title: 4  Discussion
section: 4.7 Conclusion
text:
4.7 Conclusion
Deep SiMLR establishes a deductive, modular framework for multi-modal representation learning governed by the Only Linear Encoder Entrypoint (OLEE) contract. By decoupling linear Stiefel feature attribution (\(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m\)) from downstream cross-view consensus topologies, Riemannian quasi-Newton solvers (SiMLR-LBFGSB, SiMLR-LBFGS), non-linear decoders (LEND), and detached-prior normalizing flows (Flow-SiMR-V), the architecture eliminates the clinical transparency penalty (\(\nabla_{\mathbf{X}_m} \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{V}_m\)) and enables closed-form counterfactual recourse (\(\delta \mathbf{x}_m^* = \Delta \mathbf{z}_m^* \mathbf{V}_m^\top\)).
Across 324 benchmark evaluations spanning 6 real clinical/genomic/imaging cohorts and 6 synthetic manifolds, hybrid LEND (#1 consensus rank \(3.58\), \(CMC = 0.907\)), bound-constrained SiMLR-LBFGSB (#1 OLEE basis rank \(3.17\), #1 real-cohort rank \(2.50\), support \(F_1 = 0.991\)), and detached-prior Flow-SiMR-V (#3 consensus rank \(4.17\), #3 basis rank \(4.12\), #1 real-cohort consensus mean \(0.627\)) lead overall performance, while NSAFlow-PCA (\(0.040\text{s}\)) matches dense PCA in speed while enforcing \(25.0\%\) disjoint sparsity with zero crosstalk. Every OLEE-constrained architecture significantly outperforms unconstrained deep autoencoders (NED, NEDPP, \(p_{\text{Holm}} \le 7.5 \times 10^{-4}\)). In ADNI-MCI (\(N=1,084\)), bipartite target alignment and cognitive mediation unlock a \(+47\%\text{–}58\%\) gain in MRI-only cognitive factor prediction (CogPC1 R^2 \(= 0.224\text{–}0.241\)) and a \(>6\)-fold gain in predicting clinical dementia severity (\(R^2 = 0.2648, p < 10^{-15}\)).

A.3.1 Mechanistic Alignment
LEND yields an explicit orthonormal weight matrix \(\mathbf{V}_m\) mapping input features to the latent subspace:

Proteomics (rppa, \(|r| = 0.69\) with ER status): Within the proteomics modality, ER-alpha-R-V (\(|V| = 0.290\)) and GATA3-M-V (\(|V| = 0.268\)) possess the two largest weight magnitudes, followed directly by HER2-M-V (\(0.205\)), androgen receptor AR-R-V (\(0.203\)), Cyclin_E1-M-V (\(0.200\)), progesterone receptor PR-R-V (\(0.164\)), and phosphorylated ER-alpha_pS118-R-V (\(0.131\)).

title: Appendix B — Operational Implementation and Complexity
text:
B.1.1 Training Algorithm
Initialize {V_m, theta_m, phi_m}
For epoch t in 1..T:
    1. Calculate alpha_t (Stiefel mixing coefficient)
       - alpha_t = min(1.0, t / (Total_Epochs * ramp_ratio))
    2. Forward Pass:
       # Apply OLEE
       V_active = (1 - alpha_t) * V_raw + alpha_t * NewtonSchulz(V_raw)
       Z_m = Encoder(X_m, V_active, theta_m)
       
       # For NEDPP: Disentangle Shared vs Private
       U_shared, P_private = Split(Z_m)
       Loss_disentangle = CovariancePenalty(U_shared, P_private)
       
    3. Consensus Estimation:
       - U_hat = Average(Z_1, ..., Z_M) or NewtonSchulzConsensus(Z_list)
    4. Calculate Total Energy J:
       - J = (1 - alpha_t) * L_recon + alpha_t * L_align + gamma * L_disentangle
    5. Backpropagate gradients to {V_raw, theta_m, phi_m}
    6. Update weights via Optimizer (Adam with weight decay)

B.2 Mathematical Derivations

B.2.1 Riemannian Updates
We implement Riemannian updates on the Stiefel manifold via projection onto the tangent space \(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{V}} \mathbb{V}_{k,n}\). We compute the Riemannian gradient \(\text{grad} \mathcal{J}(\mathbf{V})\) from the Euclidean gradient \(\nabla \mathcal{J}(\mathbf{V})\): \[ \text{grad} \mathcal{J}(\mathbf{V}) = \nabla \mathcal{J}(\mathbf{V}) - \mathbf{V} \text{sym}(\mathbf{V}^\top \nabla \mathcal{J}(\mathbf{V})) \]
The orthogonal penalty \(\mathcal{P}(\mathbf{V}) = \frac{1}{4} \| \mathbf{V}^\top \mathbf{V} - \mathbf{I}_k \|_F^2\) permits a Taylor expansion for a perturbation \(\Delta\): \[ \mathcal{P}(\mathbf{V} + \Delta) \approx \frac{1}{4} \text{Tr}\left( (\mathbf{V}^\top \Delta + \Delta^\top \mathbf{V})^2 \right) \] This penalty evaluates to zero for any \(\Delta\) strictly within the tangent space.


B.2.2 Newton-Schulz Convergence
We enforce orthogonality via the iteration sequence: \[ \mathbf{Y}_{k+1} = \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{Y}_k (3\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{Y}_k^\top \mathbf{Y}_k) \] The residual error \(\mathbf{E}_k = \mathbf{I} - \mathbf{Y}_k^\top \mathbf{Y}_k\) obeys the relation \(\mathbf{E}_{k+1} = \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{E}_k^2 + \frac{1}{4} \mathbf{E}_k^3\). This yields quadratic convergence: \(\| \mathbf{E}_{k+1} \|_2 < \| \mathbf{E}_k \|_2^2\).


B.2.3 Noise Reduction Law
Assuming independent noise distributions \(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_m \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \sigma^2 \mathbf{I})\), the consensus variance scales as: \[ \text{Var}\left( \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_m \right) = \frac{\sigma^2}{M} \] The corresponding \(100(1-\delta)\%\) confidence interval for the underlying signal \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) is bounded by: \[ \hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\text{consensus}} \pm z_{\delta/2} \sqrt{\frac{\sigma^2}{M}(1-\rho) + \rho\sigma^2} \] The covariance term \(\rho\sigma^2\) provides the strict statistical lower bound for the multi-modal consensus error.

section: B.9 Technical Glossary
text:
B.9 Technical Glossary

Normalizing Flow: A family of deep generative models that transforms a simple probability distribution (e.g., standard multivariate Gaussian) into a complex distribution using a sequence of invertible, bijective mappings via the change-of-variables theorem.
Bijective Mapping: A mathematically exact, one-to-one and onto function. In Flow-SiMR, bijectivity guarantees that the forward mapping (encoding) and inverse mapping (decoding) preserve information perfectly with zero reconstruction error (\(\mathcal{L}_{MSE} = 0\)).
Affine Coupling Layer: The core building block of RealNVP normalizing flows. It splits the input features into two halves, copying one partition directly while scaling and translating the other half using arbitrary non-linear neural networks (which do not need to be invertible themselves).
OLEE (Only Linear Encoder Entry-point): An architectural constraint that restricts the entry layer of a deep neural network to be an orthogonal linear projection. This forms a structural information bottleneck that prevents deep layers from memorizing noise.
NSA-Flow (Non-negative Stiefel Approximating Flow): A smooth, fully differentiable optimization penalty used to constrain the linear encoder basis matrix \(\mathbf{V}_m\) to the Stiefel manifold (\(\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{I}_K\)) during backpropagation, replacing hard SVD projections.
Schur Complement: A matrix operation used to compute the conditional mean and covariance of a partitioned multivariate Gaussian distribution in closed form, enabling mathematically valid cross-view imputation.
Leave-One-Out (LOO) Topology: An optimization pathway where each view’s latent representation is aligned against a consensus target computed exclusively from all other views, preventing the model from learning trivial identity mappings.
Modality Alignment Index (MAI): A metric (typically based on Procrustes \(R^2\)) that quantifies the alignment fidelity between an individual view’s latent space and the global consensus.
Spectral Sharpness: A random-matrix-theory-based metric evaluating singular value concentrations to identify and suppress isotropic high-dimensional noise, preventing it from corrupting the consensus representation.
Classical SiMLR: Similarity-driven Multi-view Linear Reconstruction. Strictly linear baseline architecture assuming Euclidean projection of modalities.
LEND: Linear Encoder, Deep Decoder. Combines OLEE-constrained linear encoder with a deep non-linear decoder, balancing interpretability and reconstruction fidelity.
NED: Non-linear Encoder-Decoder. Applies non-linear MLP transformations to both encoder (post-OLEE) and decoder, maximizing representational capacity.
NEDPP: Non-linear Encoder-Decoder with Private Partitions. Disentangles modality-specific private variance from shared cross-modal consensus.
Flow-SiMR: Normalizing Flow Similarity-driven Multi-view Representation. Integrates bijective normalizing flows with latent consensus alignment for information-preserving multi-modal integration.
Flow-SiMR-V: Flow-SiMR with a linear projection matrix (OLEE) entry point to allow feature attribution while maintaining deep flow-based mappings.

text:
C.1 Model Formulation & Deductive Stage 5 Architecture
To resolve the “Information Masking” problem inherent in deep multi-modal normalizing flows while preserving exact input-boundary auditability, Flow-SiMR-V prepends a Stiefel-constrained Only Linear Encoder Entrypoint (OLEE) matrix \(\mathbf{V}_m \in \text{St}(k, p_m)\) to each view’s volume-preserving Normalizing Flow. This architecture establishes a globally interpretable linear bottleneck at the input boundary while retaining bijective density mapping, conditional cross-view inference, and geodesic trajectory interpolation on the \(k\)-dimensional consensus space. The normalizing flows are implemented natively in PyTorch, adapting coupling structures from the Latent-Aligned Multiview Normalizing Flows (LAMNr Flows) framework (ntustison/LAMNrFlows).

title: Appendix C — Normalizing Flow SiMR with Linear Encoder Bottleneck (Flow-SiMR-V)
text:
C.1.1 Mathematical Formulation
For each input modality \(\mathbf{X}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_m}\) (\(m = 1, \dots, M\)):

Stage 1 — Only Linear Encoder Entrypoint (OLEE) Bottleneck: \[\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m, \quad \text{subject to } \mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{I}_k\] where \(\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}\) is retracted onto the Stiefel manifold via the NSA-Flow Sylvester polar factor / Newton-Schulz flow with optional disjoint non-negative support.
Stage 5 — Low-Dimensional Bijective Normalizing Flow: \[\mathbf{Z}_m = f_{\text{flow}, m}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})\] where \(f_{\text{flow}, m}: \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k\) is a composition of RealNVP affine coupling layers with exact analytical inverse \(f_{\text{flow}, m}^{-1}\) and tractable log-determinant \(\log |\det J_{f_{\text{flow}, m}}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})|\).
Stage 2 — Consensus Mixing, Topology, and Inverse Reconstruction: \[\mathbf{U} = \mathcal{M}(\mathbf{Z}_1, \dots, \mathbf{Z}_M; \mathbf{w}), \quad \hat{\mathbf{X}}_m = f_{\text{flow}, m}^{-1}(\mathbf{U}) \mathbf{V}_m^\top\]

title: Appendix C — Normalizing Flow SiMR with Linear Encoder Bottleneck (Flow-SiMR-V)
section: C.2 Rectangular OLEE Prior Collapse & The Detached-Prior Solution
text:
C.2 Rectangular OLEE Prior Collapse & The Detached-Prior Solution
A critical theoretical difference separates square full-dimensional normalizing flows (Flow-SiMR, where \(f_{\text{flow},m}: \mathbb{R}^{p_m} \to \mathbb{R}^{p_m}\)) from rectangular OLEE-bottlenecked flows (Flow-SiMR-V, where \(\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}\) with \(k \ll p_m\) precedes \(f_{\text{flow},m}: \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k\)).

C.2.1 Why End-to-End Gaussian Prior Gradients Collapse \(\mathbf{V}_m\)
In standard normalizing flows, maximum likelihood training minimizes the negative log-likelihood under a standard isotropic Gaussian prior \(p(\mathbf{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}_k)\): \[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}; f_{\text{flow},m}) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^n \|f_{\text{flow},m}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\|_2^2 - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \log \left|\det \frac{\partial f_{\text{flow},m}}{\partial \mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin}}}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\right|
\] When \(f_{\text{flow},m}\) acts on the full ambient space \(\mathbb{R}^{p_m}\), the change-of-variables formula is exact because the mapping is square and invertible on \(\mathbb{R}^{p_m}\). However, when the rectangular projection \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m\) (\(k \ll p_m\)) precedes the flow, the change-of-variables determinant \(\log |\det J_{f_{\text{flow},m}}|\) accounts only for volume changes inside the \(k\)-dimensional subspace and contains no log-determinant term for the subspace selection \(\mathbf{V}_m\).
If \(\nabla_{\mathbf{V}_m} \mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\) is backpropagated into \(\mathbf{V}_m\), the quadratic penalty \(\frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{Z}_m\|_2^2 = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m) + \mathcal{O}(\|f_{\text{flow},m} - \text{Id}\|)\) is minimized on the compact Stiefel manifold \(\text{St}(k, p_m)\) by rotating \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto the trailing eigenvectors of \(\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m\) with the smallest eigenvalues \(\lambda_{p_m-k+1}, \dots, \lambda_{p_m}\). Because the coupling layers can trivially rescale small-variance inputs via their log-scale networks \(s_\ell(\cdot)\) to match unit variance in \(\mathbf{Z}_m\), the joint objective is minimized by discarding the leading biological variance directions and projecting onto low-variance noise axes.


C.2.2 Detached-Prior Subspace-Decoupled Optimization
To prevent rectangular prior collapse, Flow-SiMR-V enforces detached-prior subspace decoupling:

OLEE Basis Update (\(\mathbf{V}_m\)): The Stiefel basis \(\mathbf{V}_m\) is updated exclusively by the cross-view consensus alignment energy \(\mathcal{E}_{\text{align}}\) and the within-view spectral fidelity loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}} = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M \frac{\|\mathbf{X}_m - f_{\text{flow},m}^{-1}(\mathbf{Z}_m)\mathbf{V}_m^\top\|_F^2}{\|\mathbf{X}_m\|_F^2}\), while detaching \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\) at the input to the Gaussian prior penalty (\(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) = \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}.\text{detach}()\)).
Bijective Flow Update (\(f_{\text{flow},m}\)): The RealNVP coupling layers \(f_{\text{flow},m}\) are trained via \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}(f_{\text{flow},m}(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}))) + \mathcal{L}_{\text{align}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}}\), accompanied by a zero-initialized residual identity start (\(s_\ell = 0, t_\ell = 0\) at epoch 0 so \(f_{\text{flow},m}^{(0)}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) = \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\)).

In our 1,214-combination sweep on ADNI-MCI (\(N=1,084\), 4 views, bipartite graph topology), this single mathematical correction raises Flow-SiMR-V out-of-sample CogPC1 \(R^2\) from \(0.0369\) (collapsed trailing-eigenvalue subspace) to \(0.2966\) (\(+704\%\) improvement), matching linear and deep OLEE benchmarks while preserving exact flow invertibility.

section: C.4 Algorithm for Flow-SiMR-V with Detached-Prior & Delayed Gating Warmup
text:
C.4 Algorithm for Flow-SiMR-V with Detached-Prior & Delayed Gating Warmup
To stably optimize the joint-variational objective without rectangular prior collapse or early dynamic weight collapse, Flow-SiMR-V trains the linear Stiefel encoders, normalizing flows, and dynamic MAI weights using the decoupled block-coordinate procedure below:

Iteration-0 Linear Stiefel Warm Start:

Initialize \((\mathbf{V}_1^{(0)}, \dots, \mathbf{V}_M^{(0)})\) using a fast 15-iteration linear Stiefel solver (simlr / simlr_lbfgs) and initialize all RealNVP coupling layer scale/translation weights to zero so \(f_{\text{flow},m}^{(0)}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) = \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\).

Forward Pass:

Project features to the OLEE linear subspace: \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m\) for \(m=1, \dots, M\).
Apply normalizing flows: \(\mathbf{Z}_m = f_{\text{flow}, m}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})\).
Compute shared consensus coordinates \(\mathbf{U}\) (or topology-specific targets \(\mathbf{T}_m\) under star, loo, or directed/bipartite graph).

Delayed MAI Gating Schedule:

For epoch \(t < T_{\text{delayed}}\): set modality weights uniformly \(w_m = 1/M\).
For epoch \(t \ge T_{\text{delayed}}\): update \(w_m\) via temperature-scaled softmax over the cross-view Modality Alignment Index \(\text{MAI}_m\).

Detached-Prior Loss Computation & Retraction:

Evaluate Gaussian prior negative log-likelihood \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\) on \(f_{\text{flow},m}(\text{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}))\) so prior gradients update only \(f_{\text{flow},m}\).
Evaluate alignment energy \(\mathcal{E}_{\text{align}}\) and reconstruction loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}} = \frac{1}{M}\sum_m \|\mathbf{X}_m - f_{\text{flow},m}^{-1}(\mathbf{Z}_m)\mathbf{V}_m^\top\|_F^2 / \|\mathbf{X}_m\|_F^2\) end-to-end through both \(f_{\text{flow},m}\) and \(\mathbf{V}_m\).
Retract updated \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto the Stiefel manifold via NSA-Flow Sylvester polar / Newton-Schulz retraction.

D.2 Single Analysis Path and Benchmark Engine
All statistical hypothesis tests, ranking matrices, and permutation null distributions are executed via a unified module: src/pysimlr/benchmarks/deep_ranking.py. This engine implements:

Non-parametric Friedman test and Iman-Davenport \(F\) extension (Demšar (2006); Iman and Davenport (1980)).
Two-tailed Nemenyi Critical Difference (\(CD\)) computation at \(\alpha = 0.05\) (Nemenyi (1963)).
Pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Wilcoxon (1945)) with family-wise Holm-Bonferroni step-down adjustments (Holm (1979)).
Exact sign-flip permutation tests bounded by the distribution-free resolution floor.
Multi-objective Pareto frontier identification.

Consolidating all inference into deep_ranking.py ensures that the manuscript tables, figures, and text never diverge. The test suite tests/test_deep_ranking_stats.py validates the statistical calculations:

D.3.1 Block-Level Sign-Flip Permutation Floor
In statistical hypothesis testing between paired models across \(B = 12\) independent dataset blocks (where each block cell is the mean across \(N_{\text{seeds}} = 3\) replicates, following Demšar (2006)), the exact distribution-free sign-flip null distribution across the \(B = 12\) blocks consists of \(2^B = 4,096\) equally probable sign assignments: \[
p_{\text{perm}} = \frac{1}{2^B} \sum_{\mathbf{s} \in \{-1, +1\}^B} \mathbb{I}\left(\left|\frac{1}{B} \sum_{i=1}^B s_i \Delta_i\right| \ge |\bar{\Delta}|\right)
\]
For \(B = 12\) independent dataset blocks (or \(N = 10\) independent seeds in the ADNI-MCI 4-view mediation benchmark), the minimal attainable two-sided permutation \(p\)-value occurs when every block favours the same model: \[
p_{\min, B=12} = \frac{2}{2^{12}} = \frac{2}{4096} \approx 0.000488, \qquad p_{\min, N=10} = \frac{2}{2^{10}} = \frac{2}{1024} \approx 0.001953
\]
We enforce the following statistical standards throughout the manuscript:

Zero Unadjusted Pooled \(p\)-values: We completely eliminate pooled repeated-measures \(t\)-tests and unaggregated seed-rows in global Friedman/Wilcoxon tests (build_ranking_blocks). Crossing multiple seeds or hyperparameters on the same dataset does not increase dataset-level degrees of freedom.
Floor Truncation: No distribution-free permutation test can report a value below \(2/2^B\).
Dual Subspace & Localization Reporting: Global consensus prediction (\(Y\) on \(\mathbf{U}\)) and strictly linear first-layer accuracy (\(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}\)) are reported alongside ground-truth latent (\(CMC\)) and sparse support Jaccard recovery (\(\text{Support } F_1\)).

D.5 Determinism and RNG Isolation
To ensure absolute determinism across all benchmark runs:

Process RNG Isolation: Invocations of normalizing flow retractions and torch optimization loops restore CPU and CUDA generator states upon completion. No model fitting operation mutates the caller’s global random state.
Fixed Random Seeds: The primary deep ranking benchmark iterates over seeds \(42, 43, 44\) (\(N_{\text{seeds}} = 3\), with --seeds 10 configurable for extended runs up to seed \(51\)), while the ADNI-MCI 4-view mediation benchmark evaluates across 10 seeds (\(42, \dots, 51\)). Data synthesis, train/test splitting (\(70/30\)), and neural network parameter initialization are strictly controlled by these seed parameters.
